text: Saturday, nine AM. B-grade Gate 2207, at the foot of an old dam spillway, ringed by cameras and fans.
Mok throws an arm round Jaeha for the cameras. Today the hero of Mangwon Market walks in first, with Black Hound!
Then he whispers through his smile: smile, trap rat. It's the last photo anyone will take of him.
Jaeha's smile doesn't move. Then let's make it a good one, sir.
A hundred and fifty thousand are watching Bomi's stream, and some of the chat smells something off.
Mok has ordered the streamer to stay outside, for her safety. Fine, says Bomi. She stays outside. Her drone doesn't.
Sora strolls past with a wink. His husks look sleepy today. They're saving their energy, Miss Han.
Her compass needle lies slack.
By the van, three hunters linger with cables and a black steel stake. They go in last, on a signal.
Jaeha spots the emblem on the stake. A sealing stake, with Kanghan's mark on it.
Inside: a vast drowned cathedral, knee-deep in water, bronze bells hanging silent from the vault. Jaeha wades in first, chalk in hand.
And at the edge of his vision, that tiny mark. His call, still held.
Behind him, two hunters smirk. Famous, and still walking in first like a rat.
Jaeha throws out an arm, and a blade swings out of a pillar exactly where his next step would have landed.
He chalks a neat cross beside it.
That's why they pay him, Mok beams, though there are no cameras in here. Follow his marks!
It's old trap-tester code: an arrow for the safe way, a cross for a trap. Every trap-tester reads it. So does Black Hound.
At a junction, three passages: one onward, one down into a flooded crypt, one dead end.
Jaeha chalks an arrow pointing into the crypt, with one tiny extra tick nobody would notice.
Then, with a perfectly blank face, he takes the middle passage.
Yerin whispers that the arrow pointed the wrong way. It points the way he wants someone to go.
Arrow after arrow, down the aisle.
Under a huge, ancient bell, Nib stops and stares up.
He doesn't like bells. Jaeha knows. Stay close.
Sora's needle is still slack.
She studies the two stiff husks ahead of her, amused. Asleep on purpose. Clever boy.
Next, a long side nave with a dry floor of pale and dark tiles. Jaeha stops at the threshold.
This floor is too clean, he calls; everything else here is under water. Mok tells him to walk faster.
A hunter's boot presses a dark tile. Click.
Both pairs of doors slam shut at once, and the raid is trapped between them.
Water blasts from grates high in the walls, and it's rising fast.
Two hunters haul at the doors. They don't move an inch.
Jaeha weighs it. If Borro wakes up, Sora's compass sees it. If he doesn't, they all drown.
He squeezes Borro's arm. Field form.
Across the nave, the needle snaps round to Borro.
Borro wedges his shield into the crack and heaves the doors apart, and the flood pours out in a white torrent.
Jaeha clings to a pillar, carrying sixty percent of it, his nose bleeding.
Through the gap, everyone! The Black Hound hunters scramble out past Borro, one by one.
A young hunter stops to stare at the husk. Why would it save them? Because they were drowning. Go.
Mok pushes through, soaked and furious. Sora wades out smiling at her glowing compass. There you are, big one.
Borro steps out last, and the doors grind shut behind him.
So she saw him wake. Fine. Now she thinks she knows everything.
The soaked hunters can't quite look at Borro. One bows his head to him without a word.
Mok barks at them. On your feet. It's a husk. It does what it's told.
Next, a narrow ledge high above the flooded nave, single file, with bells hanging at arm's reach.
Beside the ledge, a carved trigger, already marked with a chalk cross. A heavy bell hangs right above it.
And at the back of the line, Sora casually raises her crossbow.
Her bolt hits the trigger. The bell drops straight at Jaeha's head.
He takes one calm step aside, and it crashes past his shoulder. His husks don't even twitch.
Far below, it hits the water, and one deep toll booms through the whole cathedral.
Sora's needle hangs perfectly slack.
Jaeha turns politely. That one was marked, Miss Han. Please read the marks. Her hand slipped, she laughs.
The raid rests in a dry chapel. Mok huddles with the sealers. And Nib is nowhere to be seen.
Jaeha seems to doze. Through the link, he sees what Nib sees: a narrow crack behind the altar, and moving air.
Nib slips back out with cobwebs on his ears and sits down as if he never left. Found it.
Jaeha doesn't even open his eyes. Good.
The boss room is next. Mok will do it again, won't he, Yerin whispers. Yes. And this time Jaeha is counting on it.
He presses a stub of chalk into her hand. When the door closes, stay with Borro. Don't freeze. She doesn't anymore.
In his earpiece, Bomi. Her drone is still live, four hundred and ten thousand watching. Where does he want it?
It nests in the moss on Borro's shell, its lens peeking out between two white flowers.
The end of the nave. Tall bronze doors under a rose window, and a silent bell above them.
And a lamp, burning red.
Mok heaves a door open and bows. After you, hero.
Of course, sir. Summons go first. Then summoners.
Jaeha, Nib, Borro and Yerin wade into a dark round chamber. In the middle, something huge sits slumped and still.
Behind them, the doors swing shut. In the last strip of red light, Mok smiles, and a sealer lifts the stake.
Jaeha is calm. Again, sir? He was hoping Mok would.
